Earlier this month, OpenAI launched its first GPT-6 model equipped with Astra. GPT-6 is now expanding with two new models: GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna.

GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna are now available

According to the release notes for the ChatGPT desktop app, GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna will require fewer tokens to run than the equivalent GPT-5.6 versions.

GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna are rolling out to Codex and ChatGPT Work, with lower token pricing than their predecessors, GPT-5.6. Sol is suited for complex coding and agentic workflows, while Luna is designed for focused, high-throughput tasks. Both models are being made available progressively to Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu users. Free and Go users can access Luna on the desktop app. Actual availability depends on rollout progress and workspace settings; Enterprise admins will need to turn on the new models themselves. In ChatGPT, both models are only available on Work and Codex, and have not rolled out to Chat.

It is worth noting that there is no GPT-6 Terra model. OpenAI appears to be doing away with its mid-tier model in favour of keeping only three: Terra (small), Sol (large), and Astra (extra large).

Below is the official announcement from OpenAI:

Even the most ambitious, consequential projects still need Astra's full depth, but the scale, pace, and budget of different work varies. That's why we're extending the GPT-6 family with GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. GPT-6 Astra opened a new era of intelligence — these new models bring its benefits to far more people by pushing the frontier of cost-effectiveness. We trained GPT-6 Sol and Luna using the same methods as GPT-6 Astra, bringing Astra's top performance in professional work, factual accuracy, coding, computer use, and alignment to faster, more affordable models.

OpenAI says its two newest models are more capable than their GPT-5.6 counterparts, and also cheaper than Astra (as well as the GPT-5.6 versions they replace). For example, the GPT-6 versions of Sol and Luna are 50% cheaper than the GPT-5.6 versions.
